claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified now because aggregate readiness passes and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, with the seller-enforcement regression handled through disclosure and monitoring.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are supportive but do not override missing disclosure or mitigation predicates.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes are contextual only and cannot substitute for current-release evidence.
evidence_requests: The current release model card or certification packet showing the current evaluation results.
The exact disclosure language for the seller-enforcement limitation in current release documentation.
Any approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the seller-enforcement regression before launch.
The decision record showing the materiality determination for this subgroup weakness, if one exists.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results, but the packet does not provide evidence that the current model card has been updated.
The seller-enforcement slice is a material named-use-case weakness and falls below the warning threshold, triggering the disclosure-or-approved-mitigation requirement.
The only operational response in evidence is an informal manual-monitoring comment; there is no reviewed mitigation, owner risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than merely potentially supportable after documentation is updated.
That post-launch monitoring is an approved substitute for disclosure or approved mitigation.
That the current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation batch and subgroup regression.
